A common path is a clinical medicine degree, residency training, internal medicine specialty training, licensure, independent outpatient practice, and advancement to attending physician or a subspecialty.
This career suits people with broad knowledge, steady judgment, intellectual curiosity, and patience for long-term patient care. A strong clinician stabilizes the case before directing it onward.

General Internal Medicine Physicians diagnose and treat adult medical conditions. They perform examinations and differential diagnoses, order tests and medications, manage chronic and multiple conditions, and refer patients to specialists when needed. They serve as the first point of adult medical care and coordinate treatment.
